calls.prompt:
Use case: illustration-story
Asset type: portrait background for the Creation game, an offshore view of the same painted world in the two supplied reference paintings.
References: image 1 and image 2 establish opaque luminous gouache, fine selective ink, lapis sky, teal water, ochre geology, pale ivory light, and recognizable landmarks. Preserve the hooked ochre headland, its dark arched wave-cut cave at water level, and the pale Moon with its two neighboring dark craters. Use a new offshore camera, looking toward that coast from a little farther out at sea.
Scene: the familiar hooked headland is small and distant in the upper left, with a low coast and hazy mountains behind. The same pale cratered Moon hangs in the upper right. Below the distant coast lies calm unbroken teal sea. There is NO foreground island yet, and no birds, boats, people, buildings, circles, symbols or diagrams.
Composition: a tall 390:844 portrait painting (780x1688 or a larger exact proportion). Keep the distant headland and coast above about 20% of the canvas height, and mainly left of 28% of canvas width. Leave empty sea at the intended future island position: center 55% across, 26% down, about 49% of canvas width and 16% of canvas height. The lower 65% is calm medium-light sea with quiet broad painted strokes, softly reflecting warm ivory light; it must remain usable for movable game pieces. Do not make a hard horizontal blank strip or wash overlay: this is one continuous hand-painted ocean.
Strong natural coastal perspective, rich restrained gouache texture, warm/cool color relationships matching the references. No text, frame, border, UI, labels, inventory objects, glow emblems or watermark. Fully opaque.

Use case: precise-object-edit
Asset type: constructed Island life state of this exact portrait landscape.
Input image 1 is the EDIT TARGET. Keep its camera, distant hooked headland and cave, mountains, paired-crater Moon, sky, horizon, colors, dimensions and lower working sea unchanged. Image 2 is the earlier volcanic-island identity reference; image 3 its inhabited-bird identity reference; image 4 is the Variation diagram, supplying only its fine lapis branching connector and small ochre/coral difference-mark.
Add one natural low volcanic island in the empty sea, centered about 55% across and 27% down. Its complete shoreline should span approximately x30% to x80% and y24% to y34%; the weathered dark cone rises to about y20%. This is an actual landform with a wooded shore and believable contact with the ocean, not an icon, coin or circular island vignette. Match the existing painterly perspective and gouache. Pale surf gently meets its irregular rocky shoreline. No smoke or eruption.
On the sunlit wooded near shore, show three related little warm-ochre-and-cream birds, like the icon reference, perched naturally on separate low branches. Slightly emphasize their scale in this illustrated atlas so the birds remain readable on a small screen. One is above two others; the lower birds have subtly different throat markings. Between their perches is one delicate, unframed hand-drawn lapis lineage fork with a fine ivory edge, resembling the connector in image 4. It is an atlas annotation, not a glowing physical object. The fork goes from the upper bird to the two lower birds; use simple arrows and one tiny ochre difference-mark near the differently marked descendant. No song ribbons yet. No circular border, boxed diagram, cell pictures, labels, text, UI or watermark.
Keep all new island, birds and connector inside a compact rectangle around x29%–82%, y19%–35%. Everything outside this region must match image 1.
